title: Practice: bounds
intro: Ten questions. Always ask first: *what was this rounded to?* Then halve it.

questions.prompt: A number rounded to the nearest 10 is 240. Which of these could it be?
questions.explanation: 243, 238 and 235 all round to 240. 245, 245.9 and 249 round to 250 — so 245 is the upper bound but not a possible value.

questions.prompt: Complete the bounds for each rounded number.
hints: Halve the unit it was rounded to, then subtract and add.

questions.prompt: Now with decimal places and significant figures.
hints: 1 d.p. means nearest 0.1, so go 0.05 either way.
3400 to 2 s.f.: the second significant figure is in the hundreds column.

questions.prompt: A pencil is 14 cm long, correct to the nearest cm. Drag the marker to the **lower bound** of its length.
questions.explanation: $14 - 0.5 = 13.5$ cm. The full inequality is $13.5 \le p < 14.5$.

questions.prompt: Ruth says a number that rounds to 4800 **to the nearest 10** lies in $4750 \le n < 4850$. What is the correct inequality?
questions.explanation: Ruth used half of 100 by mistake. To the nearest 10 the bounds are $4800 \pm 5$. The $\le$ belongs at the lower bound, which is why d is wrong.

questions.prompt: The Burj Khalifa is 828 m tall, correct to the nearest metre. Complete the inequality for its height $h$.
A number rounded correct to the nearest 50 is 350. Which inequality shows its bounds?
The bounds for a number are $789.5 \le n < 790.5$. Which of these **could** be how it was rounded?
hints: The gap between the bounds is 1, so it was rounded to the nearest 1.
questions.explanation: The width is 1, so it was rounded to the nearest whole number: 790. And 790 to 3 s.f. is the same thing. To 1 d.p. would give a width of 0.1, and to the nearest 10 a width of 10.

questions.prompt: A rectangle measures 9 cm by 4 cm, both correct to the nearest cm. Work out the **upper bound** of its perimeter.
A rugby pitch is 68 m wide, correct to the nearest metre. What is the **minimum** width it could be?
hints: The minimum is the lower bound.

questions.prompt: A number rounded to 2 s.f. is 520. Jenna says it lies in $515 \le n \le 524$. Give a number that is **not** in Jenna's interval but does round to 520 to 2 s.f.
hints: Jenna has stopped at 524. What about numbers between 524 and 525?
questions.explanation: Any number from just above 524 up to (not including) 525 works — for example 524.5 or 524.9. The correct bounds are $515 \le n < 525$.
